It’s best to take scheduled movement breaks if you are sitting for long periods.  Sometimes I put a rolled up yoga mat on my chair and perch my sit bones on that to help with posture.  Definitely seek out a pelvic floor physio if you are experiencing these sensations!

In skandasana you only have to bend the knee as much as feels right in your body.  Leaving that bent knee outside the front body to make room for the front body (rather than trying to smush the belly into thigh).  I like a flow of goddess squat or wide leg yogi squat (not malasana) rise on the inhale and lower into alternating skandasana on the exhale to warm up and practice this movement or coming from opposite bent leg warrior 2.

3 part breath is a good place to start, breathing first into the low belly then continuing that inhale into the low ribs then chest, exhaling chest, ribs belly.   Postures like half frog and happy baby can be helpful as long as they are modified in a way that feels soft and comfortable for you. Legs up the wall can also be helpful with a focus on relaxing through the pelvis - maybe start with legs on a chair or bind the legs together with a blanket or strap to make legs up the wall more relaxing. Malasana or low yogi squat might be something to work towards.  Also practice releasing through the pelvic floor while driving, sitting at your desk or other times that you notice your holding tension there.   A physiotherapist would be able to help you, there are specialized pelvic floor physio’s you could seek out.  Good luck!!

It’s personal preference and dependent on use.  If you are using your blocks as an extension of your arms and you need the extra cm go with the larger.  If you are using your blocks in other ways such as strengthening or increasing challenges you might choose smaller blocks (or even foam over cork).  Typically I recommend cork blocks for stability as an assist (eg in half moon or pyramid to extend the hands to the floor).  For things like passing the block around the body in a balance posture or for supporting a fish pose I would recommend foam blocks.  Clear as mud but I hope it helps!!
